predictions.statement: for every prime p from 23 to 97, the law A and the shear B generate every matrix of determinant +-1 modulo p, a group of order 2p(p^2 - 1)
predictions.basis: an extrapolation of MF-71 (every tested prime to 19 except 3); if it holds, MF-71 earns its first prediction point; one failing prime refutes it

predictions.statement: A^2 and the shear B modulo 23, acting on the 24 points of the projective line over F23, keep the extended binary Golay code, built as the extended quadratic-residue code of length 24
predictions.basis: an extension of MF-77 from the prime 7 (length 8, E8) to the prime 23 (length 24, the Leech lattice through Conway's group); one failing generator refutes it

predictions.statement: the Fibonacci braid generators in the gauge F' = [[1/phi, 1/phi], [1, -1/phi]], sigma1 = diag(zeta^-4, zeta^3) and sigma2 = F' sigma1 F' with zeta = exp(pi i/5), reduced at the prime of Z[zeta_10] above 11 with zeta -> 2, phi -> 8, are s1 = [[9, 0], [0, 8]] and s2 = [[2, 5], [7, 4]] in GL2(F11), and the group they generate contains SL2(F11), of order 1320
predictions.basis: the image of the reduced Fibonacci braid representation; a full image modulo 11 is a statement about the reduction, not about the complex representation; one missing element of SL2(F11) refutes it

predictions.statement: for every odd N from 27 to 51, the Weil operator of A^2 on l2(Z/N) has period up to phase equal to the order of A^2 modulo N
predictions.basis: an extension of MF-100 from N = 3 to 25; one N where the periods differ refutes it

predictions.statement: for every prime p from 101 to 499, the order of A^2 modulo p divides (p - 1)/2 when p = 1 or 4 mod 5, and divides p + 1 but not (p + 1)/2 when p = 2 or 3 mod 5
predictions.basis: A^2 is multiplication by phi^2, of norm 1; phi in F_p when 5 is a square mod p, else phi^(p+1) = N(phi) = -1 in F_(p^2); one prime that breaks the pattern refutes it

predictions.statement: on the periodic approximant of length 987 of the Fibonacci Hamiltonian with V = 2, each of the twelve widest gaps has integrated density of states within 1.5/987 of frac(n/phi) for an integer n with |n| <= 20
predictions.basis: the gap-labeling theorem and the labels at length 377, V = 1 (Companion 222.5); one gap off its label refutes it

predictions.statement: for every pair of golden boosts A^(2m) and S A^(2n) S, S the coordinate exchange, m and n from 1 to 4, the Thomas-Wigner angle w of their composition has rational cosine and sine and is never zero
predictions.basis: the product lies in SL2(Z), tan(w/2) = (c - b)/(a + d), and the boost directions stay at arccos(3/5) (Companion 223.7); one irrational cos w or one vanishing w refutes it

predictions.statement: for every ordered pair of distinct indices from 4/3, 3/2, 2, 5/2 and 3, the quarter-wave transmittance of the Fibonacci stacks satisfies T_(k+6) = T_k for k = 0 to 30, with T_1 = T_4 and T_2 = T_5
predictions.basis: the six-cycle of the trace map at the quarter wave and its symmetry (Companion 224.2); one pair that breaks either equality refutes it

predictions.statement: on 144 sites, the approximant 89/144 of the Fibonacci chain, with V = 3 and beta = 4, the phason pump carries across each of the eight widest gaps a charge equal to minus the gap label
predictions.basis: the six gaps of Companion 225.6 and the identity of gap labels with Chern numbers; one gap whose charge differs from minus its label refutes it

predictions.statement: at V = 1.5, on the approximants of lengths 1597 and 2584, the gaps of width at least 0.02 carry the same 24 labels as at 233 to 987, each by the congruence of the counting function, and the gaps labeled 1, -1, 2, -2 keep width and center within 3 x 10^-4 of their values at 987
predictions.basis: the convergence at lengths 233 to 987 (Companion 226.4); one label, congruence or gap that differs refutes it

predictions.statement: modulo 64 and modulo 128 the trace map is a bijection of period 96 and 192, the Pisano periods of the law
predictions.basis: the periods modulo 9, 27 and 81 and the census at 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 (Companion 226.2); another period refutes it

predictions.statement: at V = 0.01 on length 1597 the gaps labeled n and -n, n = 1 to 6, have mean width within 0.05 percent and each width within 0.3 percent of 2V |sin(pi n/phi)|/(pi |n|)
predictions.model: the Fibonacci Hamiltonian, on-site potential V on a and 0 on b, periodic and antiperiodic boundary
predictions.parameters: V = 0.01; L = 1597; labels 1 to 6 by the congruence
predictions.uncertainty: pair splitting of order V, 0.17 percent at V = 0.01
predictions.failure: a pair mean off by more than 0.05 percent, or a gap by more than 0.3 percent, or a missing label

predictions.statement: the twelve strongest Fourier amplitudes of the Fibonacci chain of length 1597 are each within 10^-5 of |sin(pi n/phi)|/(pi |n|) and carry the labels 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 12, 14 and 17
predictions.model: the letter sequence of the Fibonacci word, its discrete Fourier transform
predictions.parameters: L = 1597; labels by the congruence with F_(k-1) = 987
predictions.expected: amplitudes |sin(pi n/phi)|/(pi |n|); the labels as at 987
predictions.uncertainty: finite-size deviations near 10^-5 at 987, smaller at 1597
predictions.failure: an amplitude off by more than 10^-5, or a different set of labels

predictions.statement: on 233 sites, the approximant 144/233, with V = 2 and beta = 3, the Fukui-Hatsugai-Suzuki Chern number of each of the eight widest gaps is -q to within 10^-6
predictions.basis: the six gaps at 89 sites (Companion 228.1) and the Resta windings of MF-154
predictions.model: the Kraus family of smooth potentials on the Fibonacci approximant, Bloch phase and phason on a torus
predictions.parameters: L = 233; p = 144; V = 2; beta = 3; 24 x 60 plaquettes
predictions.expected: C = -q for every gap, q from the integrated density of states p + q (144/233)
predictions.uncertainty: the lattice field strength gives integers once the plaquettes resolve the curvature; deviations below 10^-6
predictions.failure: a gap with |C + q| >= 10^-6, or a non-integer C
predictions.convergence: the same integers at 24 x 60 and at a finer grid
predictions.verification: the Resta winding of the polarization over the phason, as in MF-154

predictions.statement: for the nine cubic-phase states sum_k w^(c k^3)|k>/3, c = 0 to 8, the Wigner negativity is equal within each pair c, -c, is 0 at c = 0, and takes one common value on the six units c = 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8
predictions.basis: the negativity 0.5863 at c = 1 (Companion 229.6); the symmetries k -> u k and complex conjugation relate c to c u^3 and to -c, and the common value on all units goes beyond them
predictions.model: the discrete Wigner function of the nine-level system, phase-point operators D(s) Pi D(s)^dagger
predictions.expected: 0 at c = 0; one value on c = 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8; equal values within c = 3, 6
predictions.failure: a pair c, -c with different negativity, a nonzero value at c = 0, or two units with different values
predictions.convergence: exact up to floating point; no limit is taken
predictions.verification: the Wigner function computed by a second convention, the parity operator built from the Fourier transform

predictions.statement: at N = 81 the quantum cat map U_N(j, k) = w^(j^2 - jk + k^2/2)/sqrt(N) has 81 distinct eigenvalues, each a root of unity of order dividing 108, and its literal period is 108
predictions.basis: the simple-spectrum theorem (MF-185) and the literal periods at 3, 9 and 27 (Companion 230.3, 230.4)
predictions.model: the explicit quantum cat map of Companion 230.4
predictions.expected: 81 distinct eigenvalues; each a 108th root of unity; U^108 = I and no smaller power the identity
predictions.uncertainty: floating point, eigenvalue gaps well above 10^-6
predictions.failure: a repeated eigenvalue, an eigenvalue off the 108th roots, or a literal period other than 108
predictions.convergence: a finite computation; no limit is taken
predictions.verification: the commutant dimension, 81 orbits of A^2 on the 6561 labels, computed exactly

non_equivalences.statement: the 24 positions cannot be placed on the 24 heptagons of the Klein quartic in any way the law respects: PGL2(F7) has no element of projective order 24
commuting is not correspondence: A and [[0,1],[1,7]] are joined by 663,552 bijections with the same cycle type and by no linear map
the law has no conserved linear quantity; it conserves Q^2
Construction A of the Golay code is the Niemeier lattice A1^24, not the Leech lattice
the Lee-Yang model and the Fibonacci anyons share a fusion ring and are different theories: the first is non-unitary
I + C^12 + C^-12 on E8 is not the 2 x 2 law; it is the polynomial in the Coxeter element that takes the law's two eigenvalues
Euclidean rhythms equal the Fibonacci chain only up to rotation, not letter for letter
the law A and its power A^5 on the 81 states: no invertible linear map joins them (trace 1 against 2), though both are laws of the same ring
the law A and its square A^2 as permutations of the 81 states: no relabeling joins them, cycle types 1, 8, 24, 24, 24 against 1, 4, 4, 12, 12, 12, 12, 12, 12
two golden boosts whose powers agree modulo 9 are not the same boost: n and n + 6 give the same residue on the 729 states and gamma 7/2 against 710647/2
SL2(Z) holds no Lorentz rotation of order 5: its elliptic traces are 0 and +-1, rotations of order 2 and 3, while SL2(Z[phi]) holds the rotation of order 5 by 72 degrees
the residue modulo 9 of an integer trace orbit does not determine whether the orbit is bounded: (1, 1, 1) is fixed and (1, 1, 10) escapes
the on-site Fibonacci model at E = 0 is not on the six-cycle that light, sound and the off-diagonal model share: its letter matrices are not traceless
the trace map and the law share their period modulo 9, 27 and 81 and not modulo 3: 12 against 8
the law modulo 9 and the trace map modulo 9 share the period 24 and not the orbit-length distribution: 1, 8, 24, 24, 24 against 55 orbits of eight lengths
the trace map's period differs from the law's Pisano period at every prime from 5 to 31, by factors from 21 to about 6 x 10^18
the integer p of a gap label carries no topology: gaps with p = 1, 0, -1, -2, 2 have Chern numbers set by q alone
the 81 states, the phase space (Z/9)^2 of one nine-level system, are not the phase space (Z/3)^4 of two qutrits: elements of order 9 against order 3
the classical bound 2 and the quantum maximum sqrt5 of the KCBS test differ by phi^-3: no noncontextual assignment of values reproduces the quantum statistics of one qutrit
